title: PI-AMFM: Permutation-Invariant Learning for Variable-Cardinality AM-FM Mode Decomposition in Biomedical Signal Analysis
abstract: arXiv:2610.00819v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Physiological recordings often contain nonstationary oscillatory components whose number and dynamics vary across signals. Amplitude- and frequency-modulated (AM-FM) representations are well suited to characterizing such dynamics and have shown broad utility in biomedical signal analysis. Recent approaches have incorporated neural networks to learn mode decomposition patterns from data, but component cardinality is often predefined or determined through separate stopping or selection mechanisms. We propose a permutation-invariant neural framework for variable-cardinality AM-FM mode decomposition (PI-AMFM). PI-AMFM combines a multiscale temporal encoder, Mamba backbone, and component-presence estimation, with permutation-invariant Hungarian matching during training. translated_title: PI-AMFM：面向生物医学信号分析中可变分量数AM-FM模式分解的排列不变学习
translated_abstract: 生理信号记录通常包含非平稳的振荡成分，其数量和动态特性随信号而变化。幅度-频率调制（AM-FM）表示非常适合刻画此类动态特性，并在生物医学信号分析中展现出广泛的实用性。近期的方法已将神经网络引入以从数据中学习模式分解规律，但分量数量通常是预先定义的，或需通过单独的停止或选择机制来确定。我们提出了一种用于可变分量数AM-FM模式分解的排列不变神经框架（PI-AMFM）。PI-AMFM结合了多尺度时间编码器、Mamba骨干网络和分量存在性估计，并在训练过程中采用排列不变的匈牙利匹配。在合成AM-FM信号上，PI-AMFM相比对比方法取得了更低的分解误差、瞬时频率误差、重构误差和模式数量误差，同时保持了……（原文摘要此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出PI-AMFM框架，通过结合多尺度时间编码器、Mamba骨干网络、分量存在性估计及排列不变匈牙利匹配，实现了无需预定义分量数量的可变分量数AM-FM模式分解，在生物医学信号分析中取得了更优的分解性能。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes PI-AMFM, a permutation-invariant neural framework combining a multiscale temporal encoder, Mamba backbone, component-presence estimation, and Hungarian matching to achieve variable-cardinality AM-FM mode decomposition without predefined component counts, outperforming existing methods in biomedical signal analysis.
